title: Building the AI Economy: What Happens After the Data Centre Peak
gist: Oxford Economics forecasts global data centre construction work done peaking at US$212bn (2023 prices) in 2030 and then falling 40% by 2037 as building slows to long-run digital demand; Europe peaks first (2028) and plateaus, Asia in 2029 on an Australian boom, and the Americas last (2030, elevated to 2032) but with the steepest drop.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts global data centre construction work done to peak at US$212bn (2023 constant prices) in 2030 and then fall 40% by 2037 as new construction slows to the pace of long-run digital demand.
insights.speaker: Adric Kam
insights.so_what: The AI-capex construction tailwind has a visible end date; contractors and materials suppliers face a post-2030 cliff.

insights.claim: The post-2030 decline in data centre construction reflects a reversion from a build-out boom to the slower pace of long-run digital demand, rather than a collapse in digital demand itself.
insights.speaker: Adric Kam
insights.so_what: Distinguish AI demand from construction intensity — operators can keep growing while builders shrink.

insights.claim: Europe's data centre construction is expected to peak first in 2028 and then plateau, with Germany and the Netherlands contracting after 2027.
insights.speaker: Adric Kam
insights.so_what: European data centre construction exposure rolls over earliest — but falls least after the peak.

insights.claim: Asia's data centre construction is forecast to peak in 2029, driven by a boom in Australia.
insights.speaker: Adric Kam
insights.so_what: Australian construction and data centre developers are the near-term Asian beneficiaries, with a 2029 top.

insights.claim: The Americas will be the last region to peak in data centre construction, in 2030, and stay elevated until 2032 due to lengthy large-campus builds, but will then see the most substantial decline of any region.
insights.speaker: Adric Kam
insights.so_what: US exposure is the longest-lived but carries the deepest post-2032 drawdown risk.
insights.locator: The Americas will peak last in 2030

insights.claim: US construction contractors may face a sharp decline in data centre work after 2032, requiring a shift of investment toward growing regions.
insights.speaker: Adric Kam
insights.so_what: Watch US engineering/construction firms' data-centre backlog concentration and geographic diversification beyond 2032.
insights.quote: contractors in the US may face a sharpdecline in work after 2032

insights.claim: Market maturity, project types and regulatory environments will determine the timing and depth of each region's data centre construction cycle.
insights.speaker: Adric Kam
insights.so_what: Use maturity, project mix and regulation as the lenses for which regions top early vs late.
